name: Luxury Salvage Deals Platform
tag: Find luxury salvage cars worth rebuilding and see repair costs and likely margin before you bid.

scenarios.title: Price one salvage car
scenarios.ask: A salvage luxury sedan with {damage} damage is at ${bid}. Clean retail is ${retail}. Is it worth rebuilding?
steps: Photo reader
Read the sample auction photos and listed likely damaged parts for {damage} damage.
Repair estimator
Estimated parts and labor at ${=round(retail * damage)}.
Value model
Rebuilt titles often sell below clean value. Used a sample 25% discount: ${=round(retail * 0.75)}.
Fees
Added sample buyer, transport and inspection fees of ${=round(1500 + bid * 0.08)}.
Deal check
Worked out profit or loss at your bid and the highest bid for a 15% margin.

result.title: Deal estimate
rows: Estimate from sample data; inspect before you buy

followups: Why is flood damage priced so high?
Water can reach wiring, modules and interior parts that don't show in photos. The estimator adds more hidden-damage risk for flood cars.
How firm is the repair estimate?
It is a starting point from photos and sample parts prices. A hands-on inspection often moves it, which is why the max bid keeps a 15% margin.

scenarios.title: Scan this week's auctions
scenarios.ask: Scan {listings} luxury salvage listings this week and find deals under my ${budget} budget.
steps: Scanner
Read {listings} sample listings and dropped {=round(listings * 0.55)} with frame or airbag damage flags.
Estimator
Priced repairs on the remaining {=listings - round(listings * 0.55)}.
Filter
Kept cars with an all-in cost under ${budget} and at least {margin} estimated margin.
Ranker
Ranked the shortlist by margin and parts availability.

result.title: Weekly shortlist
rows: Sample listings; results vary week to week

followups: Frame and structural repairs are costly and can make a car harder to insure and resell. You can turn this filter off.
Can it watch for one model?
Yes. Save a search by make, model and year, and the scanner alerts you when a match appears.

scenarios.title: Plan parts for a rebuild
scenarios.ask: Source parts for a rebuild needing {parts} parts. I want to spend no more than ${cap}.
steps: Parts lister
Built a list of {parts} parts from the damage report.
Price checker
Compared sample new, used and aftermarket prices for each part.
Budget fit
With a {mix} mix, the sample parts total is ${=round(parts * 520 * mix)}.
Lead time
Flagged {=max(1, round(parts * 0.15))} parts with lead times over two weeks.
followups: Are used parts a good idea?
For trim and body panels often yes. For safety parts like airbags and seatbelts, the plan defaults to new parts.
How do slow parts affect the deal?
Each week a car waits ties up cash. The plan orders the {=max(1, round(parts * 0.15))} slow parts first.
